newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds Commission banana import measures.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Commission banana import measures.

text.p: The European Court of Justice dismissed on Tuesday six separate but related challenges from Belgium and Germany to European Commission measures permitting banana imports from third countries into the EU.

The Commission enacted a series of transitional measures to assist banana importers, hurt by Hurricane Debbie, and also to ease transition for those importers operating in the new EU states of Sweden, Finland and Austria.

In the event of exceptional circumstances, like Hurricane Debbie, the European Commission has the authority to enact measures impacting the quota system established by the Council of the European Union under the common banana regime, the court said.

The court found the Commission is uniquely qualified to enact measures to compensate for natural disasters, as "only the Commission is in a postion to keep track of agricultural market trends and to act quickly when necessary."

The regulations contested by Germany allow additional imports to operators supplying the Community with bananas from Martinique, Guadeloupe (Community regions) and Saint Lucia and Dominica (ACP states)

The dispute between Belgium and the Commission involved quota allocations for Austria, Finland and Sweden, countries who were not yet part of the EU when the common banana market was established in 1993.

Although the Act of Accession brought the new member states under the common agricultural policy, it also provided for the adoption of transitional measures necessary to facilitate the transition to membership, the court reasoned.

"It must be held that the factual and legal situation in the new members states was different from that prevailing in the member states of the Community of Twelve and that that difference justified the adoption by the Commission of the contested regulations," the court said.

Joined Cases C-71/95, C-155/95 and C-271/95
Kingdom of Belgium v Commission, supported by French Republic
application to annul Commission regulations (EC) No3303/94 of 21 December 1994, (EC) No 479/95 of 1 March 1995 and (EC) No 1219/95 of 30 May 1995
THE COURT hereby
1. Dismisses the applications;
2. Orders the Kingdom of Belgium to pay the costs;
3. Orders the French Republic, which intervened, to bear its own costs.

Kingdom of Belgium and Federal Republic of Germany v Commission
supported by United Kingdom and the French Republic
application to annul Commission regulations (EC) No 2791/94 of 16 November 1994 and (EC) No 510/95 of 7 March 1995
THE COURT hereby
1. Dismisses the applications;
2. Orders the applicants to pay the costs;
3. Orders the interveners to bear their own costs.
